title: Ergodicity in a hole-dopped Anderson spin insulator
authors: M. S. Bahovadinov, A. A. Markov, G. V. Shlyapnikov
abstract: An interacting many-body system being localized in the presence of disorder can fail to serve as its own bath. In an electronic system, the charge and spin degrees of freedom can act as thermal baths for each other. In this paper, we study the stability of an Anderson insulator in the spin sector with respect to charge doping. We consider one-dimensional two-component fermions in a lattice with large onsite repulsion ($t-J_{XX}$ model) and with a single hole in a random magnetic field. In the absence of the hole the spin sector is localized in arbitrarily weak random magnetic fields. We argue that a single hole thermalizes the spin chain in the weak disorder limit. In this regime our numerical results indicate ergodicity of the system as a whole and delocalization of the hole. At larger magnetic fields the hole eventually localizes with a finite localization length, and the Anderson spin insulator is restored.
summary: This work examines how doping a spin Anderson insulator with a single mobile hole affects its insulating nature in the presence of disorder. The authors find that weak disorder allows the hole to delocalize the spin system, but strong disorder pins the hole, thereby restoring the original Anderson insulating state. The transition is robustly confirmed using spectral, dynamical, and localization diagnostics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the stability of an Anderson insulator in the spin sector when coupled to a mobile charge degree of freedom (a single hole) via charge doping.
main_result: The hole acts as a bath that delocalizes the spin background in the weak disorder limit, but this delocalization is suppressed, restoring the Anderson insulator state, when the hole itself localizes in the strong disorder limit.
method: The study employs theoretical analysis using the t-JXX model, analyzing real-time dynamics, spectral statistics (adjacent-gap ratio), and eigenstate localization diagnostics (fractal dimensions).
model_or_system: The system is a one-dimensional lattice of two-component fermions described by a t-JXX model, incorporating hole hopping ($H_t$), antiferromagnetic exchange ($H_J$), and a random magnetic field ($H_h$).
key_observables: Localization length ($\xi$), spectral statistics ($\langle r angle$), participation entropies ($S_q$), and mean-square displacement ($\sigma^2(t)$).
important_parameters: Disorder strength ($W$), hole hopping amplitude ($t$), and antiferromagnetic coupling ($J$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to the single-hole sector, and the model is studied at the isotropic point $J/t=1$.
figures_summary: Figures show the crossover of spectral statistics ($\langle r angle$) from Wigner-Dyson (weak disorder) to Poissonian (strong disorder), and the transition of $\sigma^2(t)$ from diffusive ($\propto t$) to saturated (finite localization length).
paper_structure: The paper develops the model Hamiltonian, analyzes the weak disorder regime where hole motion induces spin delocalization, and contrasts this with the strong disorder regime where hole localization restores the insulating state, using multiple diagnostic tools to confirm the transition.
why_interesting: The interplay between charge dynamics (hole motion) and spin localization in a disordered environment provides a rich platform for studying how mobile excitations can fundamentally alter the nature of quantum phases, relevant to disordered quantum materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic illustration of the system and the main findings. (a) Spin disordered t −JXX model doped with a single hole. (b) At weak disorder W < Wc the spin chain is thermalized by the single hole. At a stronger disorder, W > Wc, the hole localizes and the system as a whole becomes an Anderson insulator.

FIG. 2. Disorder dependence of the disorder-averaged adjacent-gap ratio ⟨r⟩for the single-hole doped disordered XX chain at t/J = 1, shown for system sizes L = {9, 13, 17}. At weak disorder the level statistics is close to the Wigner– Dyson value ⟨r⟩WD ≈0.53, indicating strong level repulsion and delocalized many-body eigenstates. With increasing disorder, ⟨r⟩decreases continuously towards the Poisson value ⟨r⟩P ≈0.386, signaling the suppression of level repulsion and onset of localization. The crossover sharpens with increasing system size, consistent with a disorder-driven localization transition of the coupled hole-spin system.

FIG. 3. Disorder dependence of the Shannon fractal dimensions obtained from the full many-body eigenstates, D (left panel), and from the hole wavefunctions, DH, (right panel) for system sizes L = 9, 11, 13. The many-body fractal dimension D is extracted from the participation entropy of the full eigenstate in the computational basis, while DH is obtained from the reduced hole probability distribution in real space. Insets: histograms of D (left) and DH (right) at weak disorder W = 2. Errorbars are smaller than the symbol sizes.
FIG. 4. Disorder dependence of the disorder-averaged Kullback–Leibler divergence ⟨KL⟩ between neighboring many-body eigenstates for system sizes L = 9, 13, 17.

FIG. 5. Real-time dynamics of the doped hole. (a) Hole probability distribution ρ(j, tmax) at the largest accessible time for disorder strengths W = 3, 6, and 9. At weak disorder the hole distribution is broad, whereas increasing W produces a progressively sharper, exponentially localized profile around the initial hole position. Shaded regions indicate statistical error. (b) Mean-square displacement σ2(t) for weak disorder W = 2 and W = 3 and different system sizes L = 27, 31, 35.
